children: Canada's main stock index posted its sharpest weekly gain in three years on Friday, adding to recent abrupt moves, as a rebound in gold and copper prices lifted metal mining shares.

ended up 412.99 points, or 1.2%, at 34,839.87, its highest closing level since November 17. For the week, the index was up 4.97%, its biggest weekly advance since October 2023, after tumbling 8.1% the prior week.
Wall Street's main indexes also ended higher as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares

"I think the market environment we're in right now, it's got a staccato pace to it," said David Wong, group chief investment officer at CIBC Global Asset Management. "It's because we're at the point in the cycle where AI profitability is sharply in scope"
"For Canada specifically, I think oil prices can have that impact because so much of our benchmark is resource-related. We've seen gold quite volatile as well," Wong said
, which includes metal mining shares, climbed 4.6%. The price of gold
was up 2.4%, extending its recovery from a 14-month low earlier in the week, while copper (HGc1) added 3.4%
settled 0.7% lower at $83.08 a barrel but still snapped a weekly losing streak. Attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure fanned concerns over Middle East supplies
Combined, the energy and materials sectors account for about one-third of the TSX's weighting
was up 2.5% and industrials (.GSPTTIN) ended 0.7% higher
Just two of the major sectors ended lower. They included consumer staples (.GSPTTCS), which were down 1%
